chunks.title: Stock
chunks.text:
Stock (learning world 1: Basics)
A stock is a small piece of a company.
Example: SAP has about 1.2 billion shares. Buy one and you own a tiny slice of SAP.
Mini game: Slice the pizza
Quiz: You buy 1 share of Siemens. What do you own? Options: A loan to Siemens / A tiny piece of Siemens / A Siemens product voucher

spoiler.text: Quiz answer: A tiny piece of Siemens

chunks.title: Bond
chunks.text:
Bond (learning world 1: Basics)
With a bond you lend money and get interest back.
Example: Lend 1,000 € at 3% for 5 years → 30 € interest every year, 1,000 € back at the end.
Mini game: Lend & collect
Quiz: What do you usually get from a bond? Options: Fixed interest / A vote at the AGM / A share of every product sold

spoiler.text: Quiz answer: Fixed interest

chunks.title: ETF
chunks.text:
ETF (learning world 1: Basics)
An ETF is a basket of hundreds of companies in one purchase.
Example: 100 € in an MSCI World ETF spreads across ~1,400 companies — Apple, Microsoft, NVIDIA and more.
Mini game: Fill the basket
Quiz: One company in your MSCI World ETF crashes 50%. Your ETF… Options: Falls about 50% / Barely moves / Is closed

spoiler.text: Quiz answer: Barely moves

chunks.title: Dividend
chunks.text:
Dividend (learning world 1: Basics)
A dividend is a part of the profit paid out to shareholders.
Example: Allianz pays a dividend per share once a year. 10 shares → 10× the dividend into your account.
Mini game: Payday
Quiz: Who receives the dividend? Options: Only employees / Everyone who owns the shares / Only the bank

spoiler.text: Quiz answer: Everyone who owns the shares

chunks.title: Market cap
chunks.text:
Market cap (learning world 1: Basics)
Market cap = share price × number of shares — the company's price tag.
Example: Price 30 € × 5 billion shares = 150 billion € market cap.
Mini game: Guess the giant
Quiz: Company A: 10 € × 10bn shares. Company B: 500 € × 100m shares. Which is bigger? Options: A (100bn) / B (50bn) / Same size

spoiler.text: Quiz answer: A (100bn)

chunks.title: Bid / Ask / Spread
chunks.text:
Bid / Ask / Spread (learning world 2: Trading mechanics)
The buy price is a bit higher than the sell price — the gap is the spread, and it costs you.
Example: Ask 100.10 €, bid 99.90 € → buy and sell right away and you lose 0.20 € per share.
Mini game: Market stall
Quiz: You buy at the ask and immediately sell at the bid. You… Options: Break even / Lose the spread / Earn the spread

spoiler.text: Quiz answer: Lose the spread

chunks.title: Market order
chunks.text:
Market order (learning world 2: Trading mechanics)
A market order buys now, at whatever the current price is.
Example: Fast, but in a jumpy market you might pay more than the price you saw.
Mini game: Speed round
Quiz: What does a market order guarantee? Options: The price / Execution / Profit

spoiler.text: Quiz answer: Execution

chunks.title: Limit order
chunks.text:
Limit order (learning world 2: Trading mechanics)
A limit order buys only at your price or better.
Example: Limit 120 € → the order fills only if the price drops to 120 € or below.
Mini game: Set the trap
Quiz: Limit buy at 50 €, price is 55 €. What happens? Options: Buys at 55 € / Waits until 50 € or lower / Cancels instantly

spoiler.text: Quiz answer: Waits until 50 € or lower

chunks.title: Stop-loss
chunks.text:
Stop-loss (learning world 2: Trading mechanics)
A stop-loss sells automatically if the price falls to a level you set.
Example: Bought at 100 €, stop at 90 € → you lose at most about 10% (plus gaps).
Mini game: Safety net
Quiz: Why set a stop-loss? Options: To limit losses / To pay lower fees / To get dividends

spoiler.text: Quiz answer: To limit losses

chunks.title: Fees & TER
chunks.text:
Fees & TER (learning world 2: Trading mechanics)
Every trade costs an order fee, and every fund charges a yearly fee (TER).
Example: 14 trades × ~5 € = 70 € gone. A 1.8% TER vs 0.2% can cost thousands over 30 years.
Mini game: Leaky bucket
Quiz: Which costs you more over 30 years? Options: TER 0.2% / TER 1.8% / No difference

spoiler.text: Quiz answer: TER 1.8%

chunks.title: Trading hours
chunks.text:
Trading hours (learning world 2: Trading mechanics)
Outside main exchange hours fewer people trade, so spreads get wider.
Example: The same order at 14:00 and at 22:00 can cost you a different price.
Mini game: Night market
Quiz: When are spreads usually widest? Options: Midday on a weekday / Late at night / They never change

spoiler.text: Quiz answer: Late at night

chunks.title: Risk vs. return
chunks.text:
Risk vs. return (learning world 3: Risk & return)
Higher possible gains always come with higher possible losses.
Example: Savings account: ~2%, almost no risk. Single tech stock: +80% or −50% in a year.
Mini game: The slider
Quiz: An offer promises 20% a year with no risk. That's… Options: A great deal / A red flag / Normal

spoiler.text: Quiz answer: A red flag

chunks.title: Volatility
chunks.text:
Volatility (learning world 3: Risk & return)
Volatility is how wildly a price swings.
Example: Tesla can move ±5% on a normal day; an MSCI World ETF usually ±1%.
Mini game: Rollercoaster
Quiz: Which usually swings more? Options: A single growth stock / A world ETF / A savings account

spoiler.text: Quiz answer: A single growth stock

chunks.title: Drawdown
chunks.text:
Drawdown (learning world 3: Risk & return)
A drawdown is how far your portfolio fell from its highest point.
Example: 10,000 € → 7,000 € is a 30% drawdown. To get back you need +43%.
Mini game: The cliff
Quiz: After a 50% drop, how much do you need to get back to start? Options: +50% / +100% / +25%

spoiler.text: Quiz answer: +100%

chunks.title: Diversification
chunks.text:
Diversification (learning world 3: Risk & return)
Don't put all your eggs in one basket.
Example: One stock collapses 90%: all-in → −90%. Spread across 10 → about −9%.
Mini game: Egg drop
Quiz: Why diversify? Options: To guarantee profit / So one bad company can't ruin you / To pay less tax

spoiler.text: Quiz answer: So one bad company can't ruin you

chunks.title: Correlation
chunks.text:
Correlation (learning world 3: Risk & return)
Some stocks tend to move together.
Example: A scandal at one carmaker often drags Mercedes, VW and BMW down together.
Mini game: Dominoes
Quiz: You own 5 car makers. Are you well diversified? Options: Yes, 5 companies / Not really — they move together / Only if they're German

spoiler.text: Quiz answer: Not really — they move together

chunks.title: Liquidity
chunks.text:
Liquidity (learning world 3: Risk & return)
Liquidity is how fast you can sell without losing value.
Example: A big stock sells in seconds. A flat can take months.
Mini game: Garage sale
Quiz: Which is most liquid? Options: Apple shares / A holiday flat / A rare painting

spoiler.text: Quiz answer: Apple shares

chunks.title: Compound interest
chunks.text:
Compound interest (learning world 4: Time & growth)
Your profit earns its own profit — it snowballs.
Example: 50 €/month at 7% for 30 years: you pay in 18,000 €, it grows to about 61,000 €.
Mini game: Snowball
Quiz: What makes compounding strongest? Options: Time / Trading often / Checking prices daily

spoiler.text: Quiz answer: Time

chunks.title: Inflation
chunks.text:
Inflation (learning world 4: Time & growth)
Inflation makes money lose buying power over time.
Example: At 3% inflation, 100 € buys only about 74 € worth of stuff after 10 years.
Mini game: Shrinking cart
Quiz: Cash under the mattress for 10 years with 3% inflation… Options: Keeps its value / Loses buying power / Grows

spoiler.text: Quiz answer: Loses buying power

chunks.title: Savings plan
chunks.text:
Savings plan (learning world 4: Time & growth)
A savings plan invests the same amount every month, automatically.
Example: 25 € every month into an ETF — no timing, no stress.
Mini game: Autopilot
Quiz: Main advantage of a savings plan? Options: You never have to decide when to buy / Guaranteed profit / No fees ever

spoiler.text: Quiz answer: You never have to decide when to buy

chunks.title: Cost-average effect
chunks.text:
Cost-average effect (learning world 4: Time & growth)
When prices are low, the same monthly amount buys more shares.
Example: Price drops 30% → your 100 € buys about 43% more shares that month.
Mini game: Sale season
Quiz: For a monthly saver, a market dip means… Options: Buying more shares cheaply / Losing the savings plan / Paying higher fees

spoiler.text: Quiz answer: Buying more shares cheaply

chunks.title: Rebalancing
chunks.text:
Rebalancing (learning world 4: Time & growth)
Rebalancing brings your portfolio back to your planned mix.
Example: Plan 70/30 stocks/bonds; after a rally it's 80/20 → sell some stocks, buy bonds.
Mini game: Balance the scale
Quiz: Stocks rallied and now are 85% instead of 70%. Rebalancing means… Options: Buying more stocks / Selling some stocks / Doing nothing ever

spoiler.text: Quiz answer: Selling some stocks

chunks.title: Investment horizon
chunks.text:
Investment horizon (learning world 4: Time & growth)
When you need the money changes how much risk you can take.
Example: Money for a flat in 2 years ≠ money for retirement in 30 years.
Mini game: Two clocks
Quiz: Money needed in 1 year should mostly be… Options: In a single stock / Safe and easy to access / In crypto

spoiler.text: Quiz answer: Safe and easy to access

chunks.title: Earnings report
chunks.text:
Earnings report (learning world 5: Reading the market)
Companies report results every quarter — prices react to how they compare with expectations.
Example: Profit +10% sounds great — but if +15% was expected, the stock can fall.
Mini game: Beat or miss
Quiz: Profit up 10%, analysts expected 15%. The stock likely… Options: Rises / Falls / Doesn't trade

spoiler.text: Quiz answer: Falls

chunks.title: Priced in
chunks.text:
Priced in (learning world 5: Reading the market)
The market often moves before the news — when it's announced, it's already in the price.
Example: A dividend hike everyone expected barely moves the price on the day.
Mini game: Too late
Quiz: Expected news is finally announced. The price… Options: Usually jumps a lot / Often barely moves / Always falls

spoiler.text: Quiz answer: Often barely moves

chunks.title: Interest rates
chunks.text:
Interest rates (learning world 5: Reading the market)
When central bank rates change, almost everything moves.
Example: Rates up → bonds more attractive, loans pricier → stocks, especially tech, often fall.
Mini game: Rate lever
Quiz: The central bank raises rates. Growth/tech stocks usually… Options: Rise / Fall / Aren't affected

spoiler.text: Quiz answer: Fall

chunks.title: Buy the rumor, sell the news
chunks.text:
Buy the rumor, sell the news (learning world 5: Reading the market)
Prices rise on hope and often fall on confirmation — or when the rumor turns out false.
Example: 'Takeover talks!' → +8%. 'Company denies talks' → −12%.
Mini game: Hype cycle
Quiz: A stock jumps 10% on an unconfirmed rumor. The risk is… Options: None / It falls if the rumor is wrong / It gets delisted

spoiler.text: Quiz answer: It falls if the rumor is wrong

chunks.title: P/E ratio
chunks.text:
P/E ratio (learning world 5: Reading the market)
P/E shows how many years of today's profit the price equals.
Example: Price 100 €, profit 5 € per share → P/E 20.
Mini game: Expensive or cheap
Quiz: Price 60 €, profit 3 € per share. P/E is… Options: 20 / 3 / 180

spoiler.text: Quiz answer: 20

chunks.title: Bull & bear market
chunks.text:
Bull & bear market (learning world 5: Reading the market)
A bull market is a long rise, a bear market a long fall (usually −20% or more).
Example: 2020: a sharp bear market in March, then a strong bull market.
Mini game: Weather forecast
Quiz: Markets fell 25% over months. That's a… Options: Bull market / Bear market / Dividend

spoiler.text: Quiz answer: Bear market

chunks.title: Taxes & allowance
chunks.text:
Taxes & allowance (learning world 5: Reading the market)
Investment profits are taxed, but there is a yearly tax-free allowance.
Example: Set a Freistellungsauftrag at your bank so profits up to the allowance stay tax-free.
Mini game: Tax shield
Quiz: Without a Freistellungsauftrag, your bank… Options: Withholds tax right away / Never taxes you / Closes your portfolio

spoiler.text: Quiz answer: Withholds tax right away

chunks.title: Stock
chunks.text:
Stock (concept card, world 1)
A stock is a small piece of a company.
Example: Buy one share of Deutsche Telekom and you own a tiny slice of Deutsche Telekom.
Quiz: You buy 1 share of Siemens. What do you own? Options: A loan to Siemens / A tiny piece of Siemens / A Siemens voucher

spoiler.text: Quiz answer: A tiny piece of Siemens

chunks.title: Market vs. limit order
chunks.text:
Market vs. limit order (concept card, world 1)
A market order buys now at any price. A limit order buys only at your price or better.
Example: Limit 30,00 € on a share at 30,20 € → your order waits until the price is 30,00 € or lower.
Quiz: What does a limit order protect you from? Options: Paying more than you planned / Any loss / Order fees

spoiler.text: Quiz answer: Paying more than you planned

chunks.title: Fees & spread
chunks.text:
Fees & spread (concept card, world 1)
Every order costs a fee, and you buy a little above and sell a little below the mid price.
Example: A 4,90 € fee is almost 5 % of a 100 € order, but only 0,5 % of a 1.000 € order.
Quiz: Why do small single orders hurt more? Options: The fixed fee is a bigger share of the amount / Small orders are taxed more / They don't

spoiler.text: Quiz answer: The fixed fee is a bigger share of the amount

chunks.title: Profit & loss
chunks.text:
Profit & loss (concept card, world 1)
Profit or loss is today's value minus what you paid, costs included.
Example: Bought for 65,05 € incl. costs, worth 66,10 € now → +1,05 € (+1,6 %), on paper until you sell.
Quiz: Your position shows −3 %. Have you lost money? Options: Only on paper, until you sell / Yes, it's gone / No, losses don't count

spoiler.text: Quiz answer: Only on paper, until you sell

chunks.title: Signal vs. noise
chunks.text:
Signal vs. noise (concept card, world 2)
Most headlines are noise. A signal is new information that changes a company's future.
Example: "Auditor can't confirm 1,9 bn €" is a signal. "Analyst on TV is excited" is noise.
Quiz: Which one is a signal? Options: A blogger says the chart looks weak / A company cuts its profit forecast / Rainy weekend in Frankfurt

spoiler.text: Quiz answer: A company cuts its profit forecast

chunks.title: Priced in
chunks.text:
Priced in (concept card, world 2)
When everyone expects a piece of news, it's already in the price before it's announced.
Example: The ECB keeps rates unchanged, as expected: the market barely moves.
Quiz: Expected news is finally announced. The price usually… Options: Jumps / Barely moves / Always falls

spoiler.text: Quiz answer: Barely moves

chunks.title: Buy the rumor, sell the news
chunks.text:
Buy the rumor, sell the news (concept card, world 2)
Prices rise on hope and often fall when the rumor is confirmed or denied.
Example: "Purchase bonus for e-cars, sources say" → car stocks +6 %. "No bonus planned" → −8 %.
Quiz: A stock jumps on an unconfirmed rumor. The risk is… Options: None / It falls if the rumor is wrong / It gets delisted

spoiler.text: Quiz answer: It falls if the rumor is wrong

chunks.title: Volatility & drawdown
chunks.text:
Volatility & drawdown (concept card, world 3)
Volatility is how wildly a price swings. Drawdown is how far it fell from its peak.
Example: From 1.000 € to 700 € is a 30 % drawdown. To get back, you need +43 %.
Quiz: After a 50 % drop, how much do you need to get back? Options: +50 % / +100 % / +25 %

spoiler.text: Quiz answer: +100 %

chunks.title: Diversification
chunks.text:
Diversification (concept card, world 3)
Don't put all your eggs in one basket.
Example: One stock collapses by 90 %: all-in → −90 %. Spread over 10 → about −9 %.
Quiz: Why diversify? Options: To guarantee profit / So one bad company can't ruin you / To pay less tax

spoiler.text: Quiz answer: So one bad company can't ruin you

chunks.title: ETF
chunks.text:
ETF (concept card, world 3)
An ETF is a basket of hundreds of companies you buy in one order.
Example: 100 € in an MSCI World ETF spreads across about 1.400 companies, for one order fee.
Quiz: One company in your world ETF crashes 50 %. Your ETF… Options: Falls about 50 % / Barely moves / Is closed

spoiler.text: Quiz answer: Barely moves

chunks.title: Compound interest
chunks.text:
Compound interest (concept card, world 4)
Your gains earn their own gains. Over time, it snowballs.
Example: 25 €/month at 7 % for 30 years: you pay in 9.000 €, it grows to about 30.000 €.
Quiz: What makes compounding strongest? Options: Time / Trading often / Checking prices daily

spoiler.text: Quiz answer: Time

chunks.title: Savings plan & cost averaging
chunks.text:
Savings plan & cost averaging (concept card, world 4)
A savings plan invests the same amount every month. When prices are low, it buys more shares.
Example: Price drops 30 % → your 25 € buy about 43 % more shares that month.
Quiz: For a monthly saver, a market dip means… Options: Buying more shares cheaply / The plan stops / Higher fees

spoiler.text: Quiz answer: Buying more shares cheaply

chunks.title: Module 1.1: Your cabinet
chunks.text:
Your cabinet: chapter in module 1 (First steps), on the web cabinet.
Current account, trading account and portfolio: what each one is for.
Welcome to your sandbox
This is the comdirect overview, copied 1:1. Everything here runs on play money.
Current account
Trading account
This is your cash for trading. It's separate from your current account, and it's empty for now.
Portfolio
Your portfolio holds the stocks and ETFs you own. Nothing yet.
Look inside
Every account has its own page.
Task: Open your portfolio.
Empty portfolio
This is where your first stock will show up, with its profit or loss.
Back to the overview
The overview is always one click away.
Task: Go back to the overview.
Sandbox button
Need more play money later? This adds some. It's a sandbox control, not a real comdirect function.

chunks.title: Module 1.2: Top up
chunks.text:
Top up: chapter in module 1 (First steps), on the web cabinet.
Move money to your trading account and confirm with photoTAN.
Money first
To buy a stock, your money has to be on the trading account.
Task: Click "Transfer" next to the current account.
From and to
From your current account to your trading account. Both are already filled in.
Amount
Let's try a small amount first.
Task: Enter 20 €.
Check and send
Every transfer is confirmed with a TAN, a one-time code.
Task: Click "Next".
photoTAN
In real life you scan this mosaic with the photoTAN app. Here, the phone next to it is simulated.
Task: Type the TAN shown on the phone and confirm.
Did it work?
Every movement of money is listed in your transactions.
Task: Open "Transactions".
Here it is
20 € left the current account and arrived on your trading account.

chunks.title: Module 1.3: Find a stock
chunks.text:
Find a stock: chapter in module 1 (First steps), on the web cabinet.
Search by name, WKN or ISIN, or browse the Aktien-Finder.
Teaches concept cards: stock
Search
Search by name, WKN or ISIN, exactly like on comdirect.
Task: Search for SAP and open it.
WKN and ISIN
Every security has two IDs: the 6-character WKN and the 12-character ISIN. Same company, no mix-ups.
Aktien-Finder
Don't know a name yet? The Aktien-Finder filters by country, index and sector.
Task: Open the Aktien-Finder.
Filter
Narrow it down by sector.
Task: Pick the sector "Telecom".
Results
One hit left.
Task: Open Deutsche Telekom.

chunks.title: Module 1.4: Read a stock page
chunks.text:
Read a stock page: chapter in module 1 (First steps), on the web cabinet.
Price, daily change, chart periods, key numbers and news.
A stock page
Let's read the page of Deutsche Telekom, top to bottom.
Price
The last price, when it was paid, and on which exchange.
Daily change
How much the price moved since yesterday's close. Green up, red down.
Chart periods
One day says little. Zoom out.
Task: Switch the chart to 1 year (1Y).
Key numbers
Yesterday's close, today's range and the 52-week range show how much the price usually moves.
News
News about the market. In this sandbox it's simulated and only about the economy, never invented company stories.

chunks.title: Module 1.5: Place an order
chunks.text:
Place an order: chapter in module 1 (First steps), on the web cabinet.
Buy or sell, quantity, exchange, market vs. limit, costs.
Teaches concept cards: order-types, fees
Open the order form
From any stock page you can go straight to the order form.
Buy or sell
You can only sell what you own. We want to buy.
Quantity
How many shares. Always whole shares here.
Task: Enter 2.
Exchange
Where the trade happens. Xetra and Tradegate are the big ones, with tight prices.
Market or limit?
Market buys now at any price. Limit buys only at your price or better.
Task: Choose "Limit".
Your limit
The most you're willing to pay per share.
Task: Enter a limit, for example today's price.
Validity
How long your order waits if the price isn't reached. "Good for day" ends at today's close.
Costs
Every order has a fee, plus a small spread.
Task: Click "Show order costs".
Look at the fee
That's the form
You know every field now. In the mission you'll do it for real, on your own.

chunks.title: Module ★: Your first stock
chunks.text:
Your first stock: mission in module 1 (First steps), on the web cabinet.
Top up and buy, on your own. Then ⏩ one week later.
Teaches concept cards: pnl

chunks.title: Module 2.1: Your trading area
chunks.text:
Your trading area: chapter in module 2 (Reading news), on the trading area / ProTrader.
A guided tour of the trading screen: everything on one screen.
The trading area
Everything on one screen, and time that moves. It's the same portfolio as in the web cabinet. After Module 2 you move on to ProTrader.
Your account
Total value, cash and profit or loss. Low on cash? Top up here.
Find a stock
Type a name, ticker or WKN, then pick the stock from the list.
Task: Search for SAP and pick it.
Chart
Candles: each one is one day. Green closed higher, red lower. Your trades show up as arrows.
Order ticket
Buy or sell, quantity, order type and costs, always in view.
Task: Enter a quantity of 5.
Positions and orders
What you own, and your limit and stop orders waiting for their price.
News
Simulated macro and sector news. Big headlines pause the time.
Time
Play moves the market day by day. Pick 1 day/s or 1 week/s.
Task: Press Play.

chunks.title: Module 2.2: Signal or noise?
chunks.text:
Signal or noise?: chapter in module 2 (Reading news), on the trading area / ProTrader.
A simulated week: three headlines, and one that hits a company it never names.
Teaches concept cards: signal-noise
A simulated week
Made-up headlines, real lessons. Watch the news and the car stocks.
Follow a carmaker
Pick a car stock to follow.
Task: Search for Volkswagen and pick it.
Play
Headlines arrive as time moves. Big ones pause the game.
Task: Press Play.
Quiz: A star investor says "Telecom stocks are boring, I sold them all". Signal or noise? Options: Signal: new information about telecom companies / Noise: one person's opinion
Keep going
Something real is coming.
Task: Press Play until the chip supplier headline appears.
Quiz: A fire stops a chip supplier's deliveries. Whose shares are hit hardest? Options: Carmakers: no chips, no cars / Telecom companies / Nobody: it's only one factory
Two days later
Watch the next headline.
Task: Press Play until the viral post appears.
Quiz: "Carmakers will all be bankrupt by Christmas!" goes viral. Signal or noise? Options: Signal: everyone is sharing it / Noise: a loud claim without facts
The takeaway
Ask two questions about every headline: is it new information, and whose business does it really change? The fire was signal, and it hit the carmakers. The podcast and the viral post were noise.

spoiler.text:
Answer: A star investor says "Telecom stocks are boring, I sold them all". Signal or noise? → Noise: one person's opinion. Nothing about any telecom business changed. An opinion is not news.
Answer: A fire stops a chip supplier's deliveries. Whose shares are hit hardest? → Carmakers: no chips, no cars. News can hit companies it doesn't name. Modern cars need hundreds of chips.
Answer: "Carmakers will all be bankrupt by Christmas!" goes viral. Signal or noise? → Noise: a loud claim without facts. Being shared a lot doesn't make it true. Nothing new happened to the business.

chunks.title: Module 2.3: The market was faster
chunks.text:
The market was faster: chapter in module 2 (Reading news), on the trading area / ProTrader.
Why expected news barely moves prices.
Teaches concept cards: priced-in
Simulated week
A simulated week with central bank news. Watch the MSCI World ETF.
Play
Everyone reads the same forecasts.
Task: Press Play until the ECB decision.
Nothing happened?
The decision was big news, but the price barely moved.
Quiz: Why didn't the ECB decision move prices? Options: Everyone expected it: it was priced in / Nobody read it / Markets were closed
Now a surprise
Keep going.
Task: Press Play.
A surprise moves prices
Inflation fell more than expected. This time prices moved, because it was new.

spoiler.text: Answer: Why didn't the ECB decision move prices? → Everyone expected it: it was priced in. Prices react to surprises. Expected news is already in the price.

chunks.title: Module 2.4: Rumors
chunks.text:
Rumors: chapter in module 2 (Reading news), on the trading area / ProTrader.
Buy the rumor, sell the news.
Teaches concept cards: rumor
Sources say…
Simulated: a rumor about a purchase bonus for electric cars. Watch the car stocks.
Car stocks
Pick a carmaker to follow.
Task: Search for Volkswagen and pick it.
The rumor
Let's hear it.

chunks.title: Historical replay: DAX payments company
chunks.text:
A real historical market replay. The company is shown as "DAX payments company" until the reveal.
Concept: diversification. Rule to win: Never have more than 30 % of your portfolio in one stock, and beat Alex's risk-adjusted score.
Starting budget: 1000 € play money.
Headlines:
- Payment stocks in demand: online shopping keeps growing (noise: A general trend everyone already knew. Nothing new about this company.)
- Analyst keeps 'buy' rating on DAX payments company (noise: An opinion, not new information.)
- Payments company confirms: annual results will be published on Thursday (signal: A date, not a result.)
- Auditor refuses to sign off the annual accounts: 1,9 bn € of cash cannot be confirmed (signal: Real, very bad new information about this one company.)
- The CEO of the payments company resigns (signal: The crisis is getting deeper.)
- Company: the missing 1,9 bn € most likely do not exist (signal: A quarter of the balance sheet was not real.)
- Payments company files for insolvency (signal: The share is almost worthless.)
Bot moves:
- Bot alex (buy): "They're a DAX star, what could go wrong? Everything in!" → mistake: Everything in one stock. Being in the DAX doesn't protect a company. One stock can always fail.
- Bot sam (buy): "Same as every month: the whole index."
- Bot paula (buy): "A bit of everything. I feel safe."
- Bot paula (sell): "A DAX company crashed! Sell everything, now!" → mistake: Selling everything because of one company's news. Paula doesn't even own that company. Her stocks barely moved.
- Bot max (buy): "Everyone online says it'll bounce back to 100! All in!" → mistake: Buying on hype, not on facts. "Cheap" isn't "safe". The facts said the money was gone.

spoiler.text:
This was Wirecard, June 2020.
Wirecard was the first DAX member ever to go insolvent. The share went from about 104 € to around 1 € in one week. People who had everything in it lost almost everything.

chunks.title: Historical replay: US video-game retailer
chunks.text:
A real historical market replay. The company is shown as "US video-game retailer" until the reveal.
Concept: rumor. Rule to win: Don't buy the stock after it has already doubled, and beat Max's risk-adjusted score.
Starting budget: 1000 € play money.
Headlines:
- US video-game retailer: shares jump 57 % after a well-known investor joins the board (signal: Real news, but the jump was far bigger than the news itself.)
- Online forum users pile into the heavily shorted video-game retailer (rumor: Hype, not information about the business.)
- Celebrity tech CEO posts about the stock; it doubles in one day (noise: A post is not a business result.)
- Short sellers report heavy losses; share up more than 130 % in one day (rumor: The price is driven by a squeeze and hype, not by the company.)
- Several trading apps restrict buying of the share (signal: Without new buyers, the hype loses fuel.)
- Share falls 60 % in one day as the hype fades (signal: Buy the rumor, sell the news: the latecomers paid the bill.)
Bot moves:
- Bot sam (buy): "World ETF, like every month."
- Bot paula (buy): "Big names, nice and calm."
- Bot alex (buy): "I only trust one company. All in Microsoft."
- Bot max (buy): "Everyone on Reddit is buying! All in!" → mistake: Buying on hype, not on facts. The price had already tripled on posts and forum hype. Nothing about the business had changed.
- Bot max (sell): "It's crashing! Get me out!" → mistake: Selling in panic after buying the hype. Bought high on hype, sold low in panic: the classic FOMO round trip.

spoiler.text:
This was GameStop, January 2021.
Within two weeks the share went from about 20 $ to almost 350 $ and back below 50 $. Most people who bought during the hype lost money.

chunks.title: Historical replay: German carmaker
chunks.text:
A real historical market replay. The company is shown as "German carmaker" until the reveal.
Concept: signal-noise. Rule to win:
Starting budget: 1000 € play money.
Headlines:
- Motor show in Frankfurt opens with record crowds (noise: Nice for the city, nothing new about any carmaker's business.)
- US environmental agency: German carmaker used software to cheat on diesel emission tests (signal: Real, new and serious: fines, recalls and lost trust. The share fell about 19 % in one day.)
- Carmaker admits 11 million vehicles worldwide are affected and sets aside 6,5 bn € (signal: The problem is much bigger than first thought. Another day of about −20 %.)
- Analyst on TV: "The whole auto sector is finished" (noise: A dramatic opinion. Other carmakers' businesses had not changed.)
- The carmaker's CEO resigns (signal: Expected after two days of crisis; the share even rose a little.)
Bot moves:
- Bot sam (buy): "The index, as always."
- Bot paula (buy): "Two carmakers and SAP."
- Bot paula (sell): "TV says the whole auto sector is finished! Sell Mercedes too!" → mistake: Reacting to an opinion, not to facts. The news was about one carmaker. The TV quote was opinion: noise.

spoiler.text:
This was Volkswagen, September 2015 ("Dieselgate").
The share lost about a third in a few days. Other carmakers fell less: the problem was at one company, not in the whole sector.

chunks.title: Historical replay: US chipmaker
chunks.text:
A real historical market replay. The company is shown as "US chipmaker" until the reveal.
Concept: volatility. Rule to win:
Starting budget: 1000 € play money.
Headlines:
- US chipmaker's share lost about half of its value last year (noise: Old news: already in the price.)
- AI chatbot hype lifts chip stocks (sector: A theme everyone talks about. Prices can run far ahead of profits.)
- Chipmaker expects about 11 bn $ revenue next quarter; analysts had expected about 7 bn $ (signal: A huge surprise versus expectations: the share jumped about 24 % in one day.)
- US tightens export rules for AI chips to China (sector: Sector risk: one rule hits all chip companies at once.)
Bot moves:
- Bot alex (buy): "AI is the future. Everything in!" → mistake: Everything in one stock. It may work, but the risk is the same as with any single stock. Judge the decision, not the outcome.
- Bot sam (buy): "World ETF. Boring is fine."

spoiler.text:
This was NVIDIA, 2023.
The share more than tripled in 2023, with drops of 15–20 % along the way. Alex won this round, but with the same habit he lost everything on Wirecard.

chunks.title: Historical replay: DAX index (ETF)
chunks.text:
A real historical market replay. The company is shown as "DAX index (ETF)" until the reveal.
Concept: volatility. Rule to win: Don't sell your portfolio during the crash (days 25–40), and beat Paula's risk-adjusted score.
Starting budget: 1000 € play money.
Headlines:
- DAX closes at a record high (noise: Looking back, the top. Nobody can see that in the moment.)
- Northern Italy closes towns as virus cases rise sharply (signal: The first sign the virus reaches Europe's economy.)
- Oil price collapses by about a quarter after producers fail to agree (macro: A second shock on top of the first.)
- US suspends most travel from Europe; worst day for stocks in decades (macro: Panic. The drawdown is now about 35 %.)
- Germany closes borders to several neighbours; most shops must close (macro: Close to the bottom, but nobody knows that yet.)
- ECB announces 750 bn € emergency bond-buying programme (macro: Central banks step in. The low is reached around now.)
- Germany agrees a huge rescue package for companies and workers (macro: Help arrives. Markets start to recover long before the virus is gone.)
- Lockdowns ease across Europe (macro: Prices had already risen a lot: the recovery was priced in early.)
- EU leaders agree on a 750 bn € recovery fund (macro: More support for the economy.)
- Vaccine more than 90 % effective in trial, first results show (macro: Real, surprising news: markets jumped the same day.)
- First vaccinations start in the EU (macro: By now, the DAX is back at its old high.)
Bot moves:
- Bot paula (buy): "A nice diversified start."
- Bot sam (buy): "World ETF. And then: nothing."
- Bot alex (buy): "Everyone flies. Lufthansa, all in!"
- Bot max (buy): "DAX at a record high! Everyone's getting rich. All in!" → mistake: Buying on euphoria, not on facts. A record high says nothing about tomorrow. He bought on a feeling, all in one stock.
- Bot paula (sell): "Down 35 %?! Get me out before it goes to zero!" → mistake: Selling after a big drop, near the bottom. Selling locks in the loss. Her horizon is years, not weeks.
- Bot paula (buy): "OK, it's been rising for months. Safe to get back in now!" → mistake: Buying back higher than she sold. She sold low and bought high: the cost of panic.

spoiler.text:
This was the COVID crash, February to December 2020.
The DAX fell by almost 40 % in four weeks, then was back at its record high by the end of the year. Selling at the bottom turned a temporary loss into a real one.

chunks.title: Persona: Starter
chunks.text:
Starter: Lena, 22, student. Goal: First steps with small amounts. Horizon: 10+ years.
Starts with 100 € play money and a 25 €/month savings plan in module 4. Focus: Small savings plan, compound interest, not chasing hype.
First mission: Move your 100 € from the current account to your trading account and buy any stock you like with a limit order. Make sure it fits your budget, fees included.

chunks.title: Persona: Builder
chunks.text:
Builder: The Kaya family, 34. Goal: Save for the kids and a home. Horizon: About 15 years.
Starts with 500 € play money and a 50 €/month savings plan in module 4. Focus: Diversification, ETFs, staying calm in a crash.
First mission: Move 200 € from the current account to your trading account and buy any stock or ETF you like with a limit order. Make sure it fits your budget, fees included.

chunks.title: Persona: Pre-retiree
chunks.text:
Pre-retiree: Helga, 58. Goal: Make savings work before retirement. Horizon: About 7 years.
Starts with 1000 € play money and a 100 €/month savings plan in module 4. Focus: Horizon and risk, drawdown, why "cheap" isn't "safe".
First mission: Move 400 € from the current account to your trading account and buy a first position of your choice, a stock or an ETF, with a limit order. Make sure it fits your budget, fees included.

chunks.title: Investor Simulator: Your first real salary
chunks.text:
An event in the Investor Simulator (30 years of a life, one turn per year).
Your first real salary
After rent and groceries, 4.000 € a year are yours to plan. You also have 2.000 € on the side. Split this year's money on the right, then start the year.

chunks.title: Investor Simulator: Crash: markets −34 %
chunks.text:
An event in the Investor Simulator (30 years of a life, one turn per year).
Crash: markets −34 %
A banking crisis. Your ETF fell by a third in a few weeks. Every headline says it's getting worse.
Concept: volatility
Choices:
- Sell everything: Move ETF and stocks to the cushion before it gets worse → You sold near the bottom. The loss is now real, and you're out when the market recovers.
- Hold and keep paying in: Don't look at the depot for a while → Hard to watch, but nothing is lost until you sell. Your yearly money now buys at a discount.
- Buy more with half the cushion: Shares are on sale → Brave: you bought at a discount. Just make sure the cushion still covers a broken car.

chunks.title: Investor Simulator: Markets bounce back
chunks.text:
An event in the Investor Simulator (30 years of a life, one turn per year).
Markets bounce back
The panic is over and prices climb fast. Whoever held on gets most of the loss back this year.
Concept: volatility
Choices:
- Move half the cushion into the ETF: Get back in → Back in the market. Time in the market beats timing it.
- Wait for a better moment: Maybe it drops again → Waiting feels safe, but the best days often come right after the worst ones.

chunks.title: Investor Simulator: Correction: markets −18 %
chunks.text:
An event in the Investor Simulator (30 years of a life, one turn per year).
Correction: markets −18 %
Not a crisis, just a nasty year. Prices fell almost a fifth. You've seen this before.
Concept: volatility
Choices:
- Sell everything: Move ETF and stocks to the cushion before it gets worse → You sold near the bottom. The loss is now real, and you're out when the market recovers.
- Hold and keep paying in: Don't look at the depot for a while → Hard to watch, but nothing is lost until you sell. Your yearly money now buys at a discount.
- Buy more with half the cushion: Shares are on sale → Brave: you bought at a discount. Just make sure the cushion still covers a broken car.

chunks.title: Investor Simulator: The stock everyone talks about
chunks.text:
An event in the Investor Simulator (30 years of a life, one turn per year).
The stock everyone talks about
A colleague's chip stock tripled this year. “It's going to the moon,” he says at lunch, every day.
Concept: rumor
Choices:
- Move half my ETF into it: Big bet → Now one company decides a big part of your future. Exciting, until it isn't.
- A small bet: 1.000 €: From the cushion → A small bet you can afford to lose. That's the right size for a hype.
- Pass: Stick to the plan → Hype is news everyone already knows. By the time it's lunch talk, it's priced in.

chunks.title: Investor Simulator: The hype stock collapses
chunks.text:
An event in the Investor Simulator (30 years of a life, one turn per year).
The hype stock collapses
Accounting fraud. The share loses 85 % in a week. You don't own single stocks, so it's just a headline for you.
Concept: diversification

chunks.title: Investor Simulator: You're getting married
chunks.text:
An event in the Investor Simulator (30 years of a life, one turn per year).
You're getting married
Congratulations! Now the hard question: how big?
Choices:
- Big party: 15.000 €: Everyone's invited → A day to remember. It came out of savings, so check what's left in the cushion.
- Small and lovely: 4.000 €: Family and best friends → Almost as happy, and 11.000 € keep working for you.

chunks.title: Investor Simulator: A baby is on the way
chunks.text:
An event in the Investor Simulator (30 years of a life, one turn per year).
A baby is on the way
Nappies, a bigger flat, less sleep. Your yearly money to split drops by 1.500 €, for good.

chunks.title: Investor Simulator: Promotion!
chunks.text:
An event in the Investor Simulator (30 years of a life, one turn per year).
Promotion!
You're now senior. +2.000 € a year. What do you do with it?
Concept: compound
Choices:
- Save the raise: +2.000 € a year to split → Same lifestyle, more money working. That gap compounds for decades.
- Upgrade my lifestyle: Nicer flat, nicer car: +500 € a year to split → Life feels better. Most of the raise is gone each month, though, and lifestyle rarely shrinks back.

chunks.title: Investor Simulator: You lead the team now
chunks.text:
An event in the Investor Simulator (30 years of a life, one turn per year).
You lead the team now
Another step up: +2.500 € a year.
Concept: compound
Choices:
- Save the raise: +2.500 € a year to split → Same lifestyle, more money working. That gap compounds for decades.
- Upgrade my lifestyle: Nicer flat, nicer car: +625 € a year to split → Life feels better. Most of the raise is gone each month, though, and lifestyle rarely shrinks back.

chunks.title: Investor Simulator: The car breaks down
chunks.text:
An event in the Investor Simulator (30 years of a life, one turn per year).
The car breaks down
Gearbox. The garage wants 3.500 €, and you need the car for work.

chunks.title: Investor Simulator: Laid off
chunks.text:
An event in the Investor Simulator (30 years of a life, one turn per year).
Laid off
Your company restructures. Six months without a salary: you need 6.000 € to get by, and you save only half this year.

chunks.title: Investor Simulator: A friendly advisor calls
chunks.text:
An event in the Investor Simulator (30 years of a life, one turn per year).
A friendly advisor calls
He suggests swapping your ETF for an actively managed fund. “Our experts pick the winners.” It costs 1,8 % a year instead of 0,2 %.
Concept: fees
Choices:
- Switch to the fund: Experts sound good → 1,6 % more a year sounds small. Over 20 years it eats about a quarter of your gains.
- Stay with the ETF: Low costs → Most active funds don't beat the market after fees. Low costs are a return you can count on.

chunks.title: Investor Simulator: Markets at an all-time high
chunks.text:
An event in the Investor Simulator (30 years of a life, one turn per year).
Markets at an all-time high
“Too late to buy?” asks every newspaper. Your brother-in-law is waiting for the crash.
Concept: signal-noise
Choices:
- Pause the ETF, wait for a crash: Its share goes to the cushion → Your ETF share now goes to the cushion. Highs are normal: markets set new records most years. Change it back any time.
- Keep going: Stick to the plan → A record high is noise, not a signal. Nobody can call the top.

chunks.title: Investor Simulator: Year-end bonus: 3.000 €
chunks.text:
An event in the Investor Simulator (30 years of a life, one turn per year).
Year-end bonus: 3.000 €
A good year at work. The money is on your Girokonto.
Choices:
- Invest it in the ETF: Future you says thanks → 3.000 € at 30 years old can become 15.000 € or more by 60.
- Half fun, half ETF: Balance → A treat and a habit. A balance you can keep for 30 years beats a plan you quit.
- Treat myself: Weekend in Lisbon → Fun is part of the plan too. Just not every bonus.

chunks.title: Investor Simulator: Banks pay 3 % on savings again
chunks.text:
An event in the Investor Simulator (30 years of a life, one turn per year).
Banks pay 3 % on savings again
Interest rates are up. For the next four years, your cushion earns 3 % instead of 1,5 %.

chunks.title: Investor Simulator: Inflation hits 7 %
chunks.text:
An event in the Investor Simulator (30 years of a life, one turn per year).
Inflation hits 7 %
Prices jump: food, energy, rent. Money that just sits loses buying power.
Choices:
- Move half the cushion to the ETF: Companies can raise prices → Companies pass higher prices on, so shares tend to keep up with inflation over time. Keep enough cushion for emergencies.
- Keep it safe: Cash is cash → Safe from swings, not from inflation. 10.000 € today buy about 5.500 € worth of things in 30 years at 2 %.

chunks.title: Investor Simulator: Six months of travelling?
chunks.text:
An event in the Investor Simulator (30 years of a life, one turn per year).
Six months of travelling?
Your employer offers a sabbatical. You'd save only half this year.
Choices:
- Go: South America → Memories for life. One weaker year barely shows in a 30-year plan.
- Not now: Keep saving → More money, a little less life. Both count.

chunks.title: Investor Simulator: The rent goes up
chunks.text:
An event in the Investor Simulator (30 years of a life, one turn per year).
The rent goes up
New landlord, new contract. 50 € more a month: 600 € a year less to split.

chunks.title: Investor Simulator: Your side project pays off
chunks.text:
An event in the Investor Simulator (30 years of a life, one turn per year).
Your side project pays off
The weekend hobby earns money now: +900 € a year.

chunks.title: Investor Simulator: An inheritance: 20.000 €
chunks.text:
An event in the Investor Simulator (30 years of a life, one turn per year).
An inheritance: 20.000 €
Your aunt left you 20.000 €. What do you do with it?
Concept: savings-plan
Choices:
- Invest it all in the ETF: Time in the market → Statistically the best move: money invested earlier has longer to grow.
- Dream trip, invest the rest: 8.000 € trip, 12.000 € ETF → A balance you'll remember both ways.
- Keep it in the cushion: Just in case → Very safe. Beyond a few months of costs, extra cushion mostly earns little.

chunks.text:
An event in the Investor Simulator (30 years of a life, one turn per year).
Washing machine and laptop, same week
Both die within days. 1.800 €.

chunks.text:

Your pension letter arrives
The state pension estimate: about 1.400 € a month from 67. Your depot today: 0 €.
Concept: compound
